quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalks, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the lightest traffic.
On the same side traffic is moving.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Walk on the side of the road that faces the traffic coming toward you.

questions.question: What should you do when entering the interstate on a short ramp with no acceleration lane?

options.text: Enter the far-right lane right away and speed up to match traffic flow.
Use the shoulder to speed up to match traffic.
Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic.
questions.explanation: Wait for a gap in traffic before you speed up and enter. You may need to stop while waiting for a safe gap to appear.

questions.question: How should you make room for cars entering the freeway?

options.text: Slow down.
Move to a different lane.
Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane.
questions.explanation: If possible, change lanes to create space for entering vehicles. If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed to let them enter safely.

questions.question: What should you do if there are two railroad tracks next to each other?

options.text: It is always safe to cross after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing.
After one train passes, check the other track for another train.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: After one train passes, check the other track for another train.
questions.explanation: Watch for a second train on the other track after the first one passes. Do not cross until you are sure no train is coming on either track.

questions.question: You cannot park within ____ of a fire hydrant.

options.text: 10 feet
25 feet
50 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 50 feet
questions.explanation: It is against the law to park within 50 feet of a fire hydrant.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Only use your mirrors.
Signal as you start to move into the next lane.
Signal 500 feet ahead on residential streets.
Always check your blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Cars and motorcycles hide in your blind spot. Look over your shoulder before changing lanes. Signal 100 feet before changing lanes on residential streets or 5 seconds before on a freeway.

questions.question: If an oncoming car uses high beams, where should you look?

options.text: Either side
The center
The right side
The left side

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you see the road until the other car passes.

questions.question: An oncoming driver doesn't dim their high beams. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the other car.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Glance toward the right side of the road to avoid the bright lights. This helps you see enough of the road to stay on course until the other car passes.

questions.question: How can you avoid glare from an oncoming car's headlights?

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Focus on the centerline.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Glance toward the right side of the road to avoid the bright lights. Then look ahead to check where the other vehicle is.

questions.question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?

options.text: To see around the sides of the vehicle.
Because other drivers tend to pass large vehicles quickly.
Because you will get caught in the vehicle's slipstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see around the sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: The driver of a large truck, bus, van, or vehicle with a trailer may not see you behind them. Increase your distance to see around them and see the road ahead.

questions.question: How can you avoid hydroplaning when driving in rain?

options.text: Drive at the speed you would use in good weather.
Apply brakes as soon as your car starts to skid.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When you drive too fast on wet roads, your tires can lose contact with the road. Your car will slide on top of the water. This is called hydroplaning. Driving slower in rain prevents this from happening.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:

options.text: Stop, listen, and move forward carefully.
Look to both sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
Slowly pass vehicles that appear to be stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to both sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: At places where people may cross your path or where traffic meets, look left and right to make sure nothing is coming.

questions.question: When you and other vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, what should you do?

options.text: Yield to the vehicle on your left.
Yield to the vehicle on your right.
Wait until all vehicles have left before you proceed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: When multiple vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the vehicle on your right has the right-of-way. Vehicles then proceed in the order they arrived.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly and your vehicle does not have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), what should you do?

options.text: Press and hold the brake pedal.
Pump your brakes firmly.
Tap the brakes lightly.
Release the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump your brakes firmly.
questions.explanation: Pumping the brakes is the best way to stop in an emergency. Your car will stop quickly and you can still steer.

questions.question: When a curb is painted ____, it means only short parking stops are allowed.

options.text: Yellow
Blue
White
Red

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: Painted curbs show parking rules. A white curb means only short stops are allowed.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dark street, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slow enough that you can stop within the area your headlights show.
Use high beam headlights to see vehicles ahead of you.
Keep the dashboard lights bright so other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slow enough that you can stop within the area your headlights show.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night than during the day because you cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can stop within the area lit by your headlights.

questions.question: Your vehicle's accelerator sticks open while driving on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Blow your horn.
Slam on the brakes.
Turn on your four-way flashers.
Turn off the ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If the accelerator sticks, your vehicle will keep going even if you lift your foot off the gas. Turn off the ignition by moving the key just enough to stop the engine. Be careful not to lock the steering wheel. Then apply the brakes and move to a safe area.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Watch for trucks.
Do not pass trucks.
Truck parking area ahead.
Steep hill ahead going downward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill ahead going downward.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep downhill slope is coming.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway or highway, or to make a U-turn where it is allowed.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing without flashing lights or gates, what should you do?

options.text: Cross the tracks immediately and quickly.
Always stop before crossing the tracks.
Be ready to yield to any train at the crossing.
Speed up to cross before any oncoming train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train at the crossing.
questions.explanation: Always be prepared to yield to trains at railroad crossings, especially when there are no lights or gates. Only cross when your whole vehicle can fit on the other side of the tracks. Do not shift gears while crossing because your vehicle could stall.

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way only.
There is a detour to the right because of road work.
The road ahead makes a sharp turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead makes a sharp turn.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about conditions ahead. This sign warns you to slow down for a sharp turn in the road.

questions.question: If you are following a school bus or tank truck, you should:

options.text: Pass them on the right.
Be ready to stop at railroad crossings.
Follow them more closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop at railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: School buses and tank trucks must stop at railroad crossings. Be ready to stop if you are following one of these vehicles.

questions.question: At a "Yield" sign, you must:

options.text: Let vehicles cross in front of you if they are close enough to be a problem.
Let vehicles on your right go first only.
Always slow down and keep going without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let vehicles cross in front of you if they are close enough to be a problem.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed. Let any crossing or merging vehicles go first if they are close enough to cause a crash.

questions.question: When leaving a highway, when should you slow down?

options.text: On the main road just before the exit.
When you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane early. Do not slow down until after you are in the exit lane.

questions.question: You are waiting in the intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights to get other drivers to let you through.
Go around the back of a car blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while you wait to turn left. If a car hits you from behind, this keeps you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.
